1.explanation: The main bug (missing accessible labels for tab switcher buttons in the Tabs component) requires updates to the implementation that renders those button elements. The relevant logic lives in 'packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.js' (which handles the Tabs container and tab switcher UI) and possibly also 'packages/react/src/components/Tab/Tab.js' (which handles individual tab rendering). These files define how tabs are presented, including the structure, ARIA attributes, and labeling for accessibility. Fixes will go here to ensure buttons are accessible and have associated labels as required by WCAG guidelines.
1.bug_scenario: The bug relates to accessibility violations in the Carbon Tabs component. Specifically, when the tab list switches to the button UI (on small screens), the button elements controlling the tabs do not have an associated label. This means users relying on assistive technologies (like screen readers) will not know what those buttons do, as they lack visible or programmatic labels linked through attributes such as aria-labelledby or aria-label. The IBM accessibility checker highlights these violations and points out affected users, such as those relying on screen readers or voice control.

2.explanation: The accessibility bug is specific to the Tabs component, where the tab-changing buttons are rendered. Based on the repo structure, the likely root implementation for Tabs is in packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.js, with each tab likely handled in packages/react/src/components/Tab/Tab.js. These files would need to be modified to ensure the rendered button elements inside Tabs and Tab receive the correct attributes (aria-label, aria-labelledby, or similar) to be accessible. Supporting configuration or stories (like Tabs-story.js) and tests could be reviewed, but the main bug is in the rendering logic, thus these two files are directly bug related.
2.bug_scenario: The bug concerns the accessibility of the Tabs component in the React Carbon Design System. When the screen width is reduced and the tab buttons appear, an accessibility scan reveals that these <button> elements inside the Tabs component do not have associated labels. This fails several accessibility requirements (like ARIA, WCAG) because screen readers and voice control users will not know the purpose of these buttons. The solution is to add an accessible label—via an element such as aria-label, aria-labelledby, or a visible <label>, or the title attribute. The evidence for this scenario comes from the accessibility checker screenshot highlighting the missing label problem and the explanation of who is affected and what the requirement is.
